thesis: The morning pullback-long premise has failed: last 74.36 is below the 74.9 invalidation and below the SMA20 (77.13), after a run of lower closes from the 90.87 post-earnings spike. The stock is priced for perfection (forward P/E about 47.5, EV/EBITDA about 151, operating margin about 1.6%) while growth is decelerating and the Q2 net income looks like a one-off. The tape is risk-off with 10-year yields at 5.141 (91st percentile), and beta of 2.49 means a broken support level can slide quickly toward the gap-fill zone near the 65.89 20-day low. No fresh catalyst exists, insiders are selling under a plan, and the next earnings report is outside the window, so there is nothing to stop the fade. Buying a failed setup because the long-term trend is up is a bet on a bounce that has not been confirmed.

rebuttal_to_bull: Expected bull points and answers. (1) Long-term trend intact (74.36 > SMA50 66.81 > SMA200 36.98): true, but the trade was a short-horizon pullback long with a stated stop, and that stop is broken; a rising 200-day average far below price offers no near-term support. (2) Strong balance sheet, cash 250M vs debt 29M, low dilution risk: this removes tail risk but does not justify a rich multiple, and it is unrelated to timing. (3) Analyst mean target 94.43 and a Medicare coverage ruling: the target is above the 90.87 high that already failed, and the ruling is retrospective and was priced into the 10-30 gap. (4) Light volume (vol_ratio 0.56) means an orderly fade: the ratio is from a partial day, and a fade with no buyers is not support. (5) Short interest 13.9% sets up a squeeze: it is under the 15% threshold, and squeezes need a catalyst, which the news card says is missing. The downgrade stays a stop-discipline call, not a Sell, and re-entry needs a hold of 73.39 plus an SMA20 reclaim on rising volume. Caveat: the last price is about 15 minutes delayed and the close is not final, so a late reclaim of 74.9 would weaken this case.
